description: Machine-readable catalog for the 20 Anti-Dark-Code verification capabilities.

confidence_levels.0: Every meaningful edit: static, schema, architecture, and cheap changed-slice checks.
confidence_levels.1: Completed task or slice: affected unit, contract, integration, and replay checks.
confidence_levels.2: Before merge or elevated risk: property, fuzz, monkey, mutation, performance, and focused faults.
confidence_levels.3: Scheduled, release, or high-risk: full suite, soak, full mutation, migration, platform, and broad fault matrices.

capabilities.name: Mutation testing
capabilities.purpose: Measure whether tests detect plausible code defects rather than merely execute lines.

adaptations.service-web: Mutate authorization, transaction, idempotency, and validation rules in changed high-risk modules.
adaptations.frontend: Mutate state reducers, selectors, route guards, storage adapters, and error handling, not generated UI code.
adaptations.monorepo: Run only on affected packages and high-risk shared libraries.
adaptations.library-sdk: Prioritize public API branches, compatibility paths, and serialization.
adaptations.game-simulation: Prioritize economy, combat, save, replay, content validation, and rule authority.
adaptations.mobile-native: Prioritize permission, lifecycle, bridge, secure storage, and sync rules.
adaptations.infra-as-code: Use on policy and helper code, not by mutating live plans or applying infrastructure.
adaptations.ai-data: Prioritize routing, filtering, data contracts, and deterministic pipeline logic.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Prioritize parsing, exit codes, migrations, file writes, and process control.
adaptations.small-new: Defer until meaningful tests protect real behavior.
adaptations.mixed: Select and run by runtime unit. Combine only after each unit has an honest result.

capabilities.name: Model-based stateful testing
capabilities.purpose: Generate legal action sequences, check invariants, and shrink sequence failures.
local_work: Run random, stateful, and adversarial action generators
agent_work: Define state model, preconditions, actions, and invariants

adaptations.service-web: Model transaction, account, workflow, permission, and event-consumer states.
adaptations.frontend: Combine random UI clicking with legal navigation models and adversarial boundary actions.
adaptations.monorepo: Model workflows within one runtime unit at a time.
adaptations.library-sdk: Model protocol or builder states when the API is stateful.
adaptations.game-simulation: Keep dumb, stateful, and adversarial monkeys; capture seed, world state, and actions.
adaptations.mobile-native: Model permissions, foreground/background, offline/online, deep links, and navigation.
adaptations.infra-as-code: Model plan and policy workflows only in disposable or read-only environments.
adaptations.ai-data: Model pipeline states, retries, partitions, routing, and tool-call sequences.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Model command sequences, dialogs, project state, file locks, and cancellation.
adaptations.small-new: Use only if a real workflow already exists.
adaptations.mixed: Select and run by runtime unit. Combine only after each unit has an honest result.

capabilities.name: Executable invariants
capabilities.purpose: Detect impossible states at the mutation or trust boundary that creates them.
local_work: Capture first violation with state hashes
agent_work: Choose fail, quarantine, or recovery policy

adaptations.service-web: Apply at request, event, transaction, job, persistence, authorization, and external-service boundaries.
adaptations.frontend: Apply to navigation, UI state, browser storage, API clients, feature flags, rendering, and long-session behavior.
adaptations.monorepo: Apply per package and runtime unit, then synthesize without flattening package-specific evidence.
adaptations.library-sdk: Apply to public API behavior, compatibility, serialization, examples, generated clients, and platform matrices.
adaptations.game-simulation: Apply to seeded worlds, time, RNG, saves, content, economy, projections, UI exploration, and aggregate behavior.
adaptations.mobile-native: Apply to lifecycle, permissions, native bridges, secure storage, background work, platform adapters, and device constraints.
adaptations.infra-as-code: Apply to modules, policy, plans, state, environments, IAM, and runners. Never treat apply as a routine verification step.
adaptations.ai-data: Apply to data contracts, lineage, model and prompt versions, routing, evals, batch semantics, and probabilistic outputs.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Apply to commands, exit codes, files, IPC, child processes, local state, OS behavior, and long-running sessions.
adaptations.small-new: Use the lightest useful form. Record the trigger for adding heavier tooling later.
adaptations.mixed: Select and run by runtime unit. Combine only after each unit has an honest result.

capabilities.name: Differential testing
capabilities.purpose: Compare implementations that should agree and reveal drift.
local_work: Run both implementations on identical fixtures

adaptations.service-web: Compare old/new endpoints, handlers, serializers, or database adapters.
adaptations.frontend: Compare view projections to canonical domain rules and old/new render models.
adaptations.monorepo: Compare shared library versions and parallel package implementations.
adaptations.library-sdk: Keep a simple reference implementation and compare compatibility behavior.
adaptations.game-simulation: Compare engine versus projection, old versus optimized sim, and native versus web persistence.
adaptations.mobile-native: Compare iOS/Android or native/web adapters on shared fixtures.
adaptations.infra-as-code: Compare normalized plans and policy results, never routine applies.
adaptations.ai-data: Compare pipeline, route, model, prompt, or feature versions on fixed datasets.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Compare old/new formats, platform adapters, and migration implementations.
adaptations.small-new: Candidate only when a second implementation or reference exists.
adaptations.mixed: Select and run by runtime unit. Combine only after each unit has an honest result.

capabilities.name: Metamorphic testing
capabilities.purpose: Verify required relationships between transformed inputs and outputs when exact oracles are difficult.
agent_work: State the expected relation and limits

adaptations.service-web: Test retry, idempotency, ordering, pagination, and batch-size relations.
adaptations.frontend: Test equivalent navigation paths, storage round trips, reorder-independent actions, and locale changes.
adaptations.monorepo: Test transformations at package boundaries and generated artifacts.
adaptations.library-sdk: Use algebraic, round-trip, ordering, and scaling properties.
adaptations.game-simulation: Test save-load, chunk splitting, conservation, monotonic resistance, and independent event ordering.
adaptations.mobile-native: Test lifecycle chunking, sync batching, orientation, locale, and offline round trips.
adaptations.infra-as-code: Test module composition, variable normalization, and plan invariance under irrelevant ordering.
adaptations.ai-data: Test row order, batch size, partitioning, scaling, paraphrase, and stable-filter relations.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Test file round trips, equivalent flags, ordering, and chunked processing.
adaptations.small-new: Add when exact expected output becomes costly or brittle.
adaptations.mixed: Select and run by runtime unit. Combine only after each unit has an honest result.

adaptations.ai-data: Pin model, prompt, tool schema, dataset, route, seed, and environment versions.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Control temp paths, home directory, locale, clock, child-process fixtures, and OS inputs.
adaptations.small-new: Introduce injected time and randomness before hidden globals spread.

capabilities.name: Fault injection
capabilities.purpose: Exercise environmental failure such as timeouts, partial writes, duplicate events, worker death, and resource exhaustion.
local_work: Inject reviewed faults in isolated environments

adaptations.service-web: Inject timeout, duplicate delivery, partial write, dependency loss, retry storm, and queue failure.
adaptations.frontend: Inject offline, slow network, stale cache, storage quota, tab suspension, and malformed response.
adaptations.monorepo: Inject within the owning runtime, not indiscriminately across all packages.
adaptations.library-sdk: Inject malformed input, unavailable resource, cancellation, and platform adapter failure.
adaptations.game-simulation: Inject interrupted save, missing asset, worker death, storage exhaustion, and suspended tab.
adaptations.mobile-native: Inject permission denial, background kill, low storage, network switch, and interrupted sync.
adaptations.infra-as-code: Use disposable sandboxes for provider and state faults. Never fault live infrastructure casually.
adaptations.ai-data: Inject missing partitions, malformed rows, model timeout, partial backfill, and tool failure.
adaptations.cli-desktop: Inject locked files, full disk, missing permission, child-process death, and interrupted writes.
adaptations.small-new: Defer until a real persistence or external dependency boundary exists.
